body_markdown:
Over 90% of small businesses miss out on valuable deductions each year. Are you one of them?


The IRS tax code might seem like a complex set of rules, but it’s also a powerful tool for saving on taxes. Yet most small business owners miss out on 30+ deductions they’re legally entitled to claim.


In this guide, we break down **35 powerful small business tax deductions** . Whether you’re a sole proprietor, an LLC owner, or running an S-Corp or C-Corp, this will help you save money *and* stay compliant.


***Bonus:*** **[Download](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/661ff9b7c00e059c1adbb000/68194ff660ea588ad3a46fd1_TaxGPT%202025%20Small%20Business%20Tax%20Deductions%20Cheat%20Sheet.pdf) *our free printable 2025 Small Businesses Tax Deduction Cheat Sheet now.*


## 6 Tax Deductions Most Small Business Owners Miss (But Shouldn’t)


### 1. Home Office Deduction


If you use part of your home exclusively and regularly for business, you may qualify to deduct a portion of your housing expenses (even if you rent).


There are two IRS-approved methods:


- **Simplified method** : $5 per square foot, up to 300 sq. ft. = maximum $1,500
- **Actual expense method** : Calculate your actual expenses (mortgage interest, rent, utilities, property taxes, repairs, insurance) and deduct a prorated amount based on the square footage used for business


Many fear it triggers audits, or don’t understand the “exclusive use” rule. But it’s legitimate and IRS-supported, as long as your workspace is clearly defined and used solely for business.


#### **What to Document:**


- A diagram or photo of your workspace
- Square footage breakdown
- Yearly utility, rent/mortgage, and insurance totals
- If using the actual method: receipts and bills


#### **Required Forms:**


- *Schedule C (Form 1040)*
- *Form 8829 (if using actual expenses)*


*Read more about*[how to calculate home office deductions without triggering audits](https://www.taxgpt.com/blog/calculating-home-office-deductions-without-triggering-audits) *.*


### 2. Self-Employment Tax Deduction


Self-employed individuals must pay both the employer and employee sides of FICA tax, a hefty 15.3%. Fortunately, the IRS allows you to deduct half of this amount from your adjusted gross income. This doesn't reduce your[self-employment tax](https://www.taxgpt.com/blog/self-employment-taxes-and-estimated-quarterly-payments) , but it *does* reduce the income used to calculate your regular income tax.


For example, if your self-employment tax for the year is $10,000, you can deduct $5,000 from your taxable income.


Many business owners think “self-employment tax” is non-deductible like income tax. But this deduction is unique and sits *outside* your Schedule C.


#### **Required Form:**


- *Schedule 1, Line 15 (Form 1040)*


### 3. Qualified Business Income Deduction (QBI / Section 199A)


The[QBI deduction](https://www.taxgpt.com/answer/what-is-the-qbi-deduction) allows many pass-through entities, such as sole proprietors, LLCs, partnerships, and S-Corps, to deduct up to 20% of their net qualified business income.


#### Consider this example below:


- Your net business income = $120,000
- 20% QBI deduction = $24,000
- Taxable income is reduced to $96,000 before standard or itemized deductions


**Important Rules:**


- The deduction is limited or phased out above certain income thresholds ($197,300 single / $394,600 joint for 2025, indexed for inflation)
- "Specified Service Trades or Businesses" (SSTBs), like law, health, and accounting, face phase-outs, but may still qualify with planning


One of the reasons it’s overlooked is because of confusing eligibility criteria and IRS-heavy jargon. Many tax tools don’t calculate it automatically unless you know how to input it correctly.


Required Forms:


- *Form 8995 or 8995-A, attached to Form 1040*


### 4. Section 179 Deduction & Bonus Depreciation


If your business purchased equipment, technology, vehicles, or office furniture in 2025, you may be able to deduct the entire cost this year under Section 179.


- 2025 limit: $1,250,000 for qualifying equipment
- Phase-out begins at $3,130,000 in total asset purchases
- Includes tangible personal property and “off-the-shelf” software


#### **Bonus Depreciation:**


On top of Section 179, you can apply bonus[depreciation](https://www.taxgpt.com/answer/what-is-the-depreciation-schedule-for-computers-used-for-business) (40% in 2025) to eligible property, allowing for even more upfront deductions. Many think depreciation must always be spread evenly over 5–7 years. Section 168 lets you depreciate assets faster unless you opt out of it.


#### **Vehicle Caveat:**


Passenger vehicles have limits. Heavy SUVs (>6,000 lbs) may qualify for full expensing.


Required Form:


- *Form 4562 (Depreciation and Amortization)*


### 5. The Augusta Rule (IRC Section 280A(g))


[The Augusta Rule](https://www.taxgpt.com/answer/what-is-the-augusta-rule-and-what-are-its-tax-implications) is a lesser-known gem that allows you to rent your home to your business for up to 14 days per year and deduct the rental expense, while not reporting the income personally.


Let’s understand this through an example.


You host quarterly board meetings, client offsites, or video shoots at home. Your business pays you *fair market rent* for use of your residence. You get a business deduction and owe zero personal tax on the rental income (as long as it’s 14 days or fewer).


- Fair daily rental value: $500
- Used 10 days = $5,000 business deduction
- You report $0 in income


Business owners assume renting your home = personal income. But this is one of the few *non-reportable* income sources when used correctly.


#### **What to Keep:**


- Rental agreement
- Agenda or purpose of use
- Comparable fair market rental rates


### 6. Hiring Your Children


Paying your kids a fair wage for real work (social media help, filing, packaging, etc.) allows you to shift income from your higher tax bracket to theirs and potentially pay no tax at all.


#### **Tax benefit:**


- Wages paid to your child under 18 are exempt from FICA (Social Security and Medicare taxes) if you operate as a sole proprietorship or a partnership owned only by the child’s parents. If the child is under 21, the wages are also exempt from FUTA. Corporations and partnerships with any non-parent partner don’t qualify. Once your child turns 18, FICA applies to services performed in your trade or business. Income tax withholding applies at any age.
- A dependent child can earn up to $15,300 of wages tax-free in 2025. If the child can’t be claimed as a dependent, the full $15,750 single standard deduction covers the wages instead. This applies to earned wages only. Investment or other unearned income above $2,700 is taxed at the parents’ rate under the kiddie tax rules, not the child’s.


Many assume it’s a gray area. But the IRS allows it if the work is real and paid fairly.


#### **What to Document:**


- Form-941 and W-2
- Actual payments through payroll
- Time logs and job descriptions
- Fair market value for the work


*These six deductions alone could result in tens of thousands of dollars in annual tax savings. And yet, most small business owners are missing at least three of them!*


## Essential Tax Deductions Every Small Business Should Be Claiming


These deductions form the foundation of your tax-saving strategy. They’re widely recognized, IRS-approved, and apply to almost every business across industries. Yet even these are often underclaimed or misapplied due to poor documentation or confusion around eligibility.


Here’s how to make sure you’re claiming them the right way and maximizing their value.


### Everyday Business Operations Deductions


### 7. Rent for Business Property


Rent paid for office, retail, warehouse, or studio space is fully deductible. This includes short-term leases, co-working spaces, and commercial storage.


You can also deduct rent for equipment, such as a rented printer or display booth at a tradeshow.


**Not deductible** : Rent-to-own arrangements or personal property used occasionally for business.


**What to keep on file** :


- Lease agreements
- Proof of payment (bank transfers, checks)
- Invoices for short-term rentals


### 8. Utilities


Essential utilities that power your business space are deductible. These typically include:


- Electricity and gas
- Water and trash collection
- Business internet
- Sewer and heating services


If you work from home and claim a home office deduction, utilities must be prorated based on square footage.


***Audit-proofing tip*** *: Keep all utility bills and annotate any shared-use bills for personal vs. business breakdowns.*


### 9. Internet and Phone Expenses


Phone and internet services are deductible based on the percentage used for business.


- 100% deductible if used exclusively for business (e.g., dedicated business phone line or internet in office)
- Partially deductible if shared with personal use (e.g., a personal cell phone used for business)


**What to Document** :


- Itemized phone and internet bills
- Breakdown of business use vs. personal use (consider using time logs or apps)


### 10. Business Insurance


Premiums for business-related insurance policies are fully deductible. These may include:


- General liability insurance
- Commercial property insurance
- Workers’ compensation
- Cyber liability insurance
- Professional liability (E&O)
- Business auto insurance


If you're an employer, premiums paid for group health or life insurance are also deductible.


**Not deductible** : Insurance policies where the business owner is the direct beneficiary (e.g., certain life insurance policies).


### 11. Office Supplies and Equipment


Routine office supplies and low-cost tools are fully deductible in the year they’re purchased. Examples include:


- Printer paper, ink, pens, staplers
- Postage and shipping materials
- Folders, planners, labels
- Office décor or minor desk items


For larger purchases such as desks, computers, or printers, you may need to depreciate the item unless you use Section 179 to deduct it upfront.


**What to Keep** :


- Purchase receipts
- Use records (especially for items shared with personal use)


### 12. Business Meals


Meals with clients, vendors, or staff are deductible up to 50% of the cost, provided they are:


- Not lavish or extravagant
- For a business purpose
- Attended by you or a team member


100% deductible meals:


- Office holiday parties
- Meals provided to the public for promotional purposes
- Food during company training or meetings


**For Recordkeeping** :


- Save receipts with notes on business purpose, attendees, and location
- Separate food and entertainment costs on receipts


### 13. Business Travel


Travel expenses are deductible if the trip is ordinary, necessary, and away from your tax home (overnight travel is required). This includes:


- Airfare, train, or bus tickets
- Hotel stays
- Rental cars and taxis
- Business meals while traveling
- Laundry, tips, baggage fees


**What’s Partially Deductible** :


- Mixed-use trips (business + leisure): only the business portion is deductible


**What to Track** :


- Purpose of travel
- Dates, locations, and duration
- All receipts and logs for meals, transport, and lodging


### 14. Vehicle Use (Mileage or Actual Expenses)


You can deduct either:


1. [Standard mileage](https://www.taxgpt.com/answer/if-my-employers-mileage-reimbursement-rate-is-lower-than-the-irs-standard-can-i-deduct-the-difference) rate: 70 cents per mile for 2025
2. Actual expenses: Percentage of gas, maintenance, insurance, lease payments, and depreciation


Commuting miles between home and your main business location are not deductible.


**Best Practices** :


- Use a mileage tracking app (e.g., MileIQ, Everlance)
Keep gas and service receipts for actual expense method


### 15. Repairs and Maintenance


Repairs to maintain normal operation are deductible in the year they’re made. Examples:


- Fixing a leaky sink in your office
- Replacing printer parts
- HVAC maintenance


**Not Deductible Immediately** :


Capital improvements (e.g., building an extension or installing new floors) as these must be depreciated over time.


### B. Financial, Legal, and Growth-Related Deductions


### 16. Bank Fees and Merchant Processing Charges


Deduct fees from:


- Business checking or savings accounts
- Overdraft protection or monthly maintenance
- Wire transfers
- Credit card processing (PayPal, Stripe, Square, Shopify)


### 17. Legal and Professional Services


You can deduct fees paid to:


- CPAs and bookkeepers
- Tax preparers and payroll processors
- Attorneys for business-related legal services
- Consultants or advisory services


*Note: If a service combines personal and business matters, only the business-related portion is deductible.*
